# 1.2.89 - the frame's work counted and taken out: the halos drawn once, one refresh for another player's move, the fog held still, a Despair write that renders the Monokumas' sheets alone, the glass's pulse loop, a doorway that keeps the voice room, and `game.drpg.fps()`

Stage E88 ships with this version: the frame-rate work the owner asked for after the live session of 27.10 on 1.2.85 - lag
with several players, with many Remnants, and for some players in a room where everything else was under fog - and the
voice drops (in the harness a walk through a doorway cost two reconnects; whether the table's drops were such walks is
LIVE-E88-03). C0 counts the work and adds `game.drpg.fps()`, scenario 86, `glass-sweep --frame-cost` and the
GM handbook's "When the table lags"; C1 draws the rings' and the room outline's light once into a texture; C2 makes another
player's move one token's refresh; C3 holds the fog's raster still; C4 makes a setting write render what it changed; C5
trims the glass's pulse loop; C6 keeps the voice room of a token outside every room; C7 writes the books. **The harness
counts work, it does not measure frames per second**: every number below is a count of work done (refreshes, rebuilds,
renders, pictures, voice sends and connects) or a software Chromium reading (the curtain's CSS, the pulse on synthetic
panes), and every frame-rate claim is a table's (LIVE-E88-01 to
LIVE-E88-08, Known gaps). The owner's four questions run on their defaults (Before installing, 3). CI on its last commit is in
Checked.

## Before installing

1. **Back up the world, and note the version you ran,** so a problem can be traced back.
2. **No world data changes; no migration runs.** No setting, flag, GM store, socket event or keybinding is added or removed,
   and no module hook is added. The counters and the pictures drawn once live in each browser's memory, the voice rooms
   kept through a doorway in the primary GM's; all are lost on a reload: the counters and the pictures cost at most one frame's or one
   pass's work to rebuild, and a player standing in a doorway when the primary GM reloads goes to the main room at the
   next send (read in the code, not run; LIVE-E88-03). `lang/en.json` stays at 3930 strings and `lang/pl.json` at 4735 (0 added, 0 removed, 0 reworded in each).
3. **The owner's questions, on their defaults until answered.** Q1: `fps()` may run during a session; it prints a console
   line before it starts. Q2: with "Glass blurs the map" off, the map's halos (the rings and the room outline) lose their
   blur too; with it on they look as before. Q3: a token outside every room keeps the voice room it came from. Q4: whether
   "Glass blurs the map" should start off on players' browsers comes back with the table's numbers (Known gaps).
4. **Two new console calls.** `counters()` writes nothing; `fps()` writes nothing with `{ toChat: false }`, and without it
   whispers its report to the caller, as `perf()` does. `await game.drpg.fps({ toChat: false })` watches five seconds of frames, then
   switches the module's effects off one at a time for 60 frames or one second each, whichever ends first, and puts each
   back; the map stands still for about a second at the end. A second call while one runs is refused. `game.drpg.counters()`
   reads the module's counts, `game.drpg.counters({ reset: true })` reads them and zeroes them. `game.drpg.perf()` is
   unchanged. `fps()` prints console English, as `perf()` does; no lang key changed.

## At the table

### For the GM

- **When the table lags** (GM handbook, section 20): six steps on the GM's machine and on the weakest player's - the browser
  and GPU notes, `perf()` and `fps()` standing still with a player alone under fog, the Look switches one at a time, a
  walk across three rooms with `whySlow()` and `fps()`, the GM's screen with the most Remnants, and the voice lines. Send one
  block a machine.
- **Reading `fps()`** (GM handbook, section 20): its first lines are the frame rate, the middle frame, the slowest
  twentieth and the frames over 33 and 50 ms; the canvas lines count the filters standing, the light drawn once, and
  Foundry's own filters, which `fps()` reads and never switches off; the module's work per second; then each effect held
  alone - the outline's and the rings' light each as a live filter and as its picture, the fog raster and backdrop, the
  drift, the blur, the pulse, the ticker, the endless CSS animations and the canvas last. The line with the most saved is
  the effect that costs that machine most. Then turn off, in this order, "Glass blurs the map", "Glass pulse", "State name
  behind the clock", turn "Reduced motion" on, and try the theme "Monokuma Legacy" last.
- **A doorway keeps the voice room** (GM handbook, 9.5): a player's token outside every room - a doorway square, a corridor
  not drawn as a room - keeps the voice room it came from while that room stands on its scene and floor, so a walk through
  a door changes the voice room once. A token you drag into a corridor keeps its last room too; drag it into a room to move
  its voice. A Monokuma's token outside every room goes to the main room, as before. With "Verbose console logging" on, the
  connect's Debug line says which connect of the page it was, and the primary GM's log says once when a token outside every
  room keeps its room.
- **Another player's step costs your browser that token's refresh** (C2); a GM's verdicts read no room, so on a GM's browser
  every move is that token alone. A ring whose drawing still stands is kept, not drawn again.

### For players

- **Through a door, one change of voice channel** (player handbook, Voice): standing in a doorway or in a corridor that is no
  room, you keep the channel of the room you came from until you step into another room. You also hear whoever has just
  stepped out of your room into a doorway or such a corridor.
- **If the screen stutters** (player handbook, Look): in the Look dialog, one at a time, turn "Glass blurs the map" off
  first, then "Glass pulse" and "State name behind the clock", then turn "Reduced motion" on, and last try the theme
  "Monokuma Legacy". Each changes only your own screen. If the GM asks, stand still and run
  `await game.drpg.fps({ toChat: false })` in the console (F12); it takes about twenty seconds, the effects switch off for a
  second at most each and come back by themselves, and the map stands still for a second at the end.

### For everybody

- **The rings' and the room outline's light** (C1): drawn once into a texture and worn as a picture, one texture for each
  frame shape however many tokens wear it, struck to match the live light at the zoom it was drawn (its pixels are not
  compared headless, Known gaps); between two zoom re-strikes it scales
  with the map as the line does. A light that cannot be drawn once (past the fog's texture cap, or no renderer) keeps its
  live filter. With "Glass blurs the map" off the light is drawn without its blur, live or drawn once (Q2). Under
  "Monokuma Legacy" no halo is drawn, as before.
- **The fog's drift moves in whole pixels** (C3): the masked raster and the backdrop are drawn into a picture of their own
  and drawn again only when what they show changed; the drift now steps a whole pixel six to eight times a second where it
  slid by a fraction of a pixel each frame. With "Reduced motion" on the fog stands still and is not drawn again. A pan
  draws the raster every frame, as before.
- **A Despair write renders the Monokumas' sheets alone** (C4); a minimised sheet waits and renders once on its restore; the
  status strip is built again only for the settings it reads (the clock, the overflow, the language, the overflow rules and
  the theme).
- **The glass's pulse** (C5): in headless Chromium its new loop drew 0 pixels different from the old on synthetic panes;
  whether the curtain itself looks as before is LIVE-E88-08. Its polygons are scaled once and its fill strings made once a step.
- **What the harness counted, before each change and after it** - work done, not frame time:

| where | what | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GM at rest, Stained Glass, 30 Remnants (stand-in renderer) | ring blurs live on the canvas | 34 | 0 (34 rings wear 2 textures from 2 renders) |
| another player's move, each other browser | refreshes per listener | 46 | 1 |
| another player's move, each other browser | whole visibility passes / next-frame walk | 1 / 46 | 0 / 1 |
| another player's move, each other browser | Remnant icons dressed | 30 | 0 |
| another player's move, GM | rings rebuilt / colour reads | 34 / 34 | 0 / 1 |
| a discovery ledger write, GM | rings rebuilt | 34 | 0 |
| the clock moves, GM | Remnant rings rebuilt | 60 | 30 |
| the clock moves, Stained Glass | status strip built | 3 | 1 |
| a Despair write, every browser | stand-in sheets rendered / status strip built | 2 / 1 | 1 (the Monokuma's) / 0 |
| the fog at rest, 60 frames (stand-ins) | raster and backdrop drawn | 60 mask passes | 10 pictures each |
| Gym, a square outside every room, Dorm B | voice rooms sent / connects on p1 | 2 / 2 | 1 / 1 |
| Dorm B, the same square, Dorm B again | voice rooms sent / connects on p1 | 2 / 2 | 0 / 0 |
| the pulse, 600 frames, 24 synthetic panes, headless Chromium | ms a frame (4 runs) | 38.5-65.6 | 29.7-46.9 |

  The moving player's own browser still runs the whole pass (46 refreshes) with 0 rings rebuilt. Since fix G4 the
  next-frame walk also walks every token once a second while anything refreshes, counted apart
  (`visibility.reassert.sweep`), so the walk row above is C2's count. One count went up: on p4's
  browser, under Stained Glass, a clock move rebuilds 5 rings where it rebuilt 3, from C4 on (Known gaps). The curtain's
  CSS, read by `node audit/glass-sweep.mjs --frame-cost` in software Chromium at C0, is a shape and not a table's number:
  Stained Glass 147.8 ms a frame at 1920x1080 and 38.9 with the blur held, 90.2 and 28.9 at 1366x768 - the blur 61-109 ms
  of a 90-148 ms frame; "Monokuma Legacy" 16.6-17.7 ms whatever is held.

## Known gaps

- **LIVE-E88-01** (item 323, not tried yet): `fps()` at a real v14 table, on the GM's machine and the weakest player's, both
  themes, a player alone under fog; everything looks as before after it, and a second call is refused.
- **LIVE-E88-05** (item 324, not tried yet): a token's refresh as the harness models it - how many refreshes one step and one
  drag cost a browser, and a token hidden and shown again comes back on its room's players' screens. Every canvas count
  above stands on this model, one refresh a move where v14 slides a token frame by frame.
- **LIVE-E88-02** (item 325, not tried yet): screenshots before and after of the rings' and the room outline's light, both
  themes, at play zoom and a step in, with "Glass blurs the map" off and on, and The Forge's isometric view if the table
  uses it; the same screenshots cover the fog and the pulse.
- **LIVE-E88-03** (item 326, not tried yet): the voice cut-outs named from a table's "Voice:" lines (a door, a doorway or a
  corridor, an Eclipse, a second window); one connect a door; a player in a doorway while the primary GM reloads goes to
  the main room at the next send (read in the code, not run).
- **LIVE-E88-04** (item 327, not tried yet; the stage's doneWhen): `fps()` before (1.2.85-1.2.88) and after this train on the
  GM's and the weakest player's browser, both themes, at rest, during another player's walk and with the most Remnants -
  the only measure of a frame-rate gain.
- **LIVE-E88-06** (item 328, not tried yet): the fog held as a picture - screenshots at rest, after a pan, a resize and in the
  isometric view; whether the whole-pixel drift reads as judder (the owner's call; `RASTER_STEP_MS` is the knob); "Reduced
  motion"; a scene change mid-dissolve.
- **LIVE-E88-07** (item 329, not tried yet): a Despair write on real sheets renders no student sheet; a minimised sheet
  restored shows the current values; the player's status strip during a darkening and an incident.
- **LIVE-E88-08** (item 330, not tried yet): the pulse looks as before at 1920x1080 and 1366x768, also during an Objection and
  with a waiting Call.
- **E88-10, open: the pulse's skip seldom fires.** A pane's fill moves more than one stored step a frame for most of its
  cycle: in headless Chromium the new loop drew 455 of 455 frames at 24 panes, 454 at 4 and 446 at 2, so the skip saves
  almost nothing; a job is drawn whole or not at all, not pane by pane. A real saving needs a slower pulse, a visible change -
  the owner's call.
- **E88-13, open: the repository's own command table** for whoever works on the module does not yet list `fps()` and
  scenario 86; the owner adds the two drafted rows. The books are written.
- **Q4.** Whether "Glass blurs the map" should start off on players' browsers is asked again with the table's numbers; the
  software Chromium reading above (the blur 61-109 ms of a 90-148 ms frame) is a shape, not a table's number.
- **The light drawn once.** Its pixels are not compared with the live filter's anywhere headless (no renderer); the isometric
  view is read in PIXI 7's API, not run. The reveal's own outline light keeps its live blur for the seconds a reveal plays.
  A recoloured outline takes its new colour in its light at the next re-strike, as before. The hour's repaint of every ring
  still draws the Remnants' rings again.
- **One move, one refresh.** A token whose visibility the engine writes outside its own refresh is walked again within a
  second only while some token refreshes; on a map where nothing moves it stands until the next refresh, as before C2. The
  Mastermind's lair is checked with one arrangement (Aiko the Mastermind, her lair Dorm B, Botan stepping), not with a
  Mastermind standing in a lair that is another player's room. The p4 clock count above (one more ring pass, 3 to 5) is not
  traced.
- **The fog.** The picture's pixels are not compared with the live layer's, and the hold's wiring is not run by a test
  (R1012 runs its pieces on stand-ins); the frame time saved is a table's.
- **A setting write.** Only the Despair write was narrowed: every other kind of sync still renders every open character sheet
  (E37). A minimised real sheet's render on its restore is read in Foundry's window API, run only on a stand-in.
- **The voice.** A token a GM drags into a corridor on purpose keeps its last room; a drag through a room that ends in a gap
  keeps the last room a pass read (read, not run). A GM browser that loses its connection without seeing the other GM's
  connect keeps its map until its next heartbeat (read, not run). The reconnect itself is not shortened.
- **`fps()`.** Its holds are run on planted stand-ins, not on a v14 canvas with Foundry's vision filters; what the one-second
  cap costs in noise on a 15 fps screen is not measured; `audit/perf-baseline.json` has no revision row for `perfReport`'s
  current body, so `perf()` runs have no recorded body to compare with (the owner to agree).
- Known leaks whose stages have not shipped are unchanged (8 known leaks, as at 1.2.88).
